simple.meaning: קֶמַח (qemach) is a Hebrew object word meaning “flour.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 18:6. The surrounding context includes offering, death, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קֶמַח (H7058) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: קֶמַח (qemach) / H7058 is traced through Genesis 18:6, Numbers 5:15, Judges 6:19, 1 Samuel 1:24 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said, “Quickly prepare three seahs* 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.”

majorEvents.label: Offering
majorEvents.evidenceText: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring her offering for her: one tenth of an ephah* 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel of barley meal. He shall pour no oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, for it is a meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to memory.

majorEvents.label: Death
majorEvents.evidenceText: The woman had a fattened calf in the house. She hurried and killed it; and she took flour, and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread of it.

timeline.evidenceText: Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said, “Quickly prepare three seahs* 1 seah is about 7 liters or 1.9 gallons or 0.8 pecks of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.”

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring her offering for her: one tenth of an ephah* 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel of barley meal. He shall pour no oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, for it is a meal offering of jealousy, a meal offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to memory.

Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes of an ephah † 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel of meal. He put the meat in a basket and he put the broth in a pot, and brought it out to him under the oak, and presented it.

When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls, and one ephah§ 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel of meal, and a container of wine, and brought him to Yahweh’s house in Shiloh. The child was young.
The woman had a fattened calf in the house. She hurried and killed it; and she took flour, and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread of it.
brought beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, meal, parched grain, beans, lentils, roasted grain,

She said, “As Yahweh your God lives, I don’t have a cake, but a handful of meal in a jar, and a little oil in a jar. Behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and bake it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.”
For Yahweh, the God of Israel says, ‘The jar of meal will not run out, and the jar of oil will not fail, until the day that Yahweh sends rain on the earth.’ ”
The jar of meal didn’t run out, and the jar of oil didn’t fail, according to Yahweh’s word, which he spoke by Elijah.
But he said, “Then bring meal.” He threw it into the pot; and he said, “Serve it to the people, that they may eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
Take the millstones and grind flour.

definitions.full: H7058. qemach קֶ֫מַח noun [masculine] flour, meal ; — absolute ׳ק 1Sam 1:24 +, קָ֑מַח Isa 47:2 ; construct קֶמַח Num 5:15 ; — Judg 6:19 (material for unleavened cakes), 1Sam 1:24 ; 28:24 ; 2Kin 4:41 ; defined by סֹלֶת (q. v.) Gen 18:6 , distinguished from סֹלֶת 1Kin 5:2 ; of barley ( שְׂעֹרִים ) Num 5:15 (P), but 2Sam 17:28 + קָלִי שְׂעֹרִים, חִטִּם, ; + other articles of food 1Chron2 Sam 12:41 (van d. H. 2 Samuel 12:40); kept in a) כַּד 1Kin 17:12 , 14 , 16 ; made by grinding Isa 47:2 ; ק ׳יַעֲשֶׂה צֶמַחבְּלִי Hosea 8:7 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root probably meaning to grind ;
